newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses extend gains, dollar strengthens.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses extend gains, dollar strengthens.

text.p: By Leonard Santorelli

European bourses made healthy gains on Tuesday after many hit trading records the previous day and even Paris bounced back from a poor start triggered by the strong showing of leftwing parties in parliamentary elections.

On the foreign exchange front, the dollar strengthened nearly a pfennig, with the mark slipping against other European currencies as the French poll increased expectations of a softer European single currency.
Most attention was fixed on equities after 10 European bourses, including Frankfurt and Zurich, scored trading peaks on Monday, encouraged by a big rally in Wall Street at its last session on Friday.
German stocks extended their bull run to surge to a fresh trading record of 3678.49 points in the morning session but dealers said the momentum was not accompanied by bigger trading volumes.
The star performers were steel group Thyssen AG and retailer Metro AG, both of which climbed strongly after releasing better-than-expected profit figures.
London, which was closed for a public holiday on Monday, climbed 0.7 percent in early trade, its first opportunity to react to Wall Street's record close on Friday.
The bourse put on 30.6 points to reach 4692.4 at one stage as cash-rich institutional investors looked to buy into the market. It fell back slightly by mid-morning.

A weaker bonds market and worries about higher interest rates kept many participants sidelined. "Turnover has been pathetic," the head of sales and trading at a large investment bank said. "The banks have kept us going but the key will be how Wall Street behaves."

French election jitters unsettled bond markets across Europe because of worries over the future of the European monetary union following the outcome of the surprise victory for the Socialist coalition in the first round.
"If the Socialists get back into power, the chances of EMU going ahead on time certainly will be diminished," a London trader said.

Some strategists believe the FTSE will itself scale new peaks soon, spurred on by a wall of cash that is set to flood the market with the June 2 flotation of the Halifax Building Society, Britain's biggest mortgage lender.

Paris stocks started under the cloud of the first round election results but clawed back early losses to show gains of 0.8 percent by lunch-time. The bourse plunged four percent on Monday, its biggest one-day loss in four years.
French shares opened 0.72 percent lower at 2641.88 points on the CAC-40 index but recovered as sentiment turned. Investors were awaiting President Jacques Chirac's television speech in the evening.
"People just figure that even if the left is in power, they will have to follow the discipline imposed by world financial markets," an analyst said.
In currency markets, the dollar was boosted by the fresh uncertainty over EMU following the French vote and ahead of the next round on Sunday.

"The election results suggest, if repeated next Sunday, that you are likely to get a broader grouping towards EMU, which does suggest that the euro will be a weaker currency," said Jeremy Stretch currency strategist at NatWest Markets.
A softer euro would benefit currencies outside the system such as the dollar and the Swiss franc, said analysts.

The dollar was largely unchanged against the yen from the levels seen late on Monday but analysts said the U.S. currency was still struggling to find its sense of direction after sinking last week to five-month lows below 112 yen on expectations of higher rates in Japan.
Elsewhere, the beleaguered Czech crown was hit hard after the central bank eliminated the band within which it had moved against a mark/dollar basket.
The crown was fixed at 19.5 to the mark, compared with the previous fix of 18.08, and 33.1 to the dollar, as against 30.5.
STOCK PRICES AT 1130 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was was up 21.2 points to 4,683.0.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 22.42 points at 2,677.11.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 16.50 points at 3,674.36.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6985 marks and 116.34 yen compared with 1.6899 marks and 116.33 yen in late European trade on Monday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $343.55 ounce, compared to $343.10 in late trade on Monday. Silver was unchanged at $4.75.
